title: StatusPageView
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column (inside the screen's scrolling column) of MonarchCalloutBanner, MonarchStatusBadge, MonarchUptimeBar, MonarchIncidentTimeline, MonarchTextField and MonarchButton
summary: A recipe, not a component: a status page as an in-app screen, with the overall state, each service's state and history, the active incident's updates and a subscribe field.
whenToUse: In an app's help or settings area, to show whether the product works now and what is being done about an incident.
whenNotToUse: For one service's history, use MonarchUptimeBar. For an incident's updates alone, use MonarchIncidentTimeline. For a public status website, use the web component.
api: MonarchUptimeBar(segments = history, startLabel = "30 days ago", endLabel = "Today", size = MonarchUptimeBarSize.Sm)
MonarchTextField(value = email, onValueChange = { … }, label = "Email") and MonarchButton(text = "Subscribe", onClick = { … })

options.name: overall
options.description: The overall state from the app's server: the callout's tone, title and message.

options.name: services
options.type: List of name, MonarchStatusDefinition and List<MonarchUptimeBarSegment>
options.description: Each service with its current state and daily history, oldest first.

options.name: updates
options.description: The active incident's updates; leave the section out when there is none.

options.name: onSubscribe
options.description: The app's call to subscribe an email to updates; leave the section out without one.

states.name: all operational
states.description: A success callout, every service Operational, no incident section.

states.name: degraded or down
states.description: A warning or danger callout, the affected services' badges, and the incident's updates in a live timeline.

states.name: subscribed
states.description: The app replaces the field with a confirmation line.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component: the toned callout, toned status badges with their labels, uptime bars in their status colors with a text summary, and the incident timeline. Section titles use the heading style. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's StatusPageView is one component with a header, stats, grouped services, maintenance, active and past incidents, a legend and a subscribe form, laid out for a wide page. On Android it is a recipe for one scrolling screen: the overall callout first, then services one per row with a compact uptime bar under each, then the active incident and subscribe. Stats, maintenance windows and past incidents are further sections the app adds with the same components (past incidents in a MonarchCollapsible). iOS has the same plan: a recipe.
accessibility: Section titles use the heading style, which MonarchText marks as a heading.
Each service's state is a status badge with its label in words, never color alone; each uptime bar has a spoken summary.
The incident timeline is live, so new updates are announced.
edgeCases: With many services, group them under headings or in collapsibles.
Times in the timeline follow the time zone the app passes.
A day without checks is a segment without uptime: the bar shows no data.
